title: False Sharing of Contiguous Array Elements
pattern: Independent variables mutated frequently by separate threads residing within the same physical cache line (typically 64 bytes).
why_bad: Writing to one variable invalidates the adjacent thread's cache line, causing massive invalidation traffic and "ping-ponging" cache misses even though the threads share no logical variables.
detection: Array of structures or contiguous memory buffers accessed concurrently by different threads using separate indices.
counterexample: The elements are purely read-only and never modified after initialization. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Use alignment directives (`#[repr(align(64))]`) or pad structure elements so that distinct variables are mapped to distinct cache lines.
source: *Herlihy - Art of Multiprocessor Programming*, Appendix B (p. 135 / 138) and *Rust For Rustaceans*, Chapter 11 (p. 143 / 434).
